judgments.reasoning_cat1: Eligibility turns on 'six months of priority in the shop', using 'priority' where seniority might be meant, and the notice conditions are strict but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-A.1(b) defines priority as promotional order rather than length of service, so 'six months of priority' is hard to apply against that definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The band table's 'More Than / Fewer Than' columns leave gaps (e.g., between 76 and 75, 118 and 117), and days 0–33 earn nothing without saying so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It incorporates 13-B's day-counting rules, and 13-K.3 folds paid-leave days back into the same schedule — a circularity worth noting but not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not be taken in such a manner as to interfere with adequate staffing' is an undefined limit sitting against the flat right to take accumulated leave 'at any time during the term'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 20-A prescribes the rate for unused leave payouts in different terms ('normal straight-time weekly pay' versus 'the then prevailing rate'), a genuine inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single crediting sentence, dense but with a determinate effect on the day counts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It enlarges the contribution base under 13-H.1 and 13-I.1 (which speak of 'each shift worked'), so paid-leave days counted as worked days is a direct interaction and a plausible dispute point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow, clear rule about holidays falling in paid leave.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-B.4 has the analogous rule for holidays in vacation but pays a day's straight-time rather than merely not counting the day, a difference in treatment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise two-week crediting cap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the National Guard rule in 13-B.2 for vacation credits; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For cause' is left undefined while the procedural requirements are precise; the text is also badly corrupted in places.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15 speaks of discharge 'without just cause', a different formulation, and 16-M.3 excepts discharges from the no-change rule — the 'cause'/'just cause' mismatch is a real interpretive seam.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Every effort' is a soft duty and 'to that extent the provisions ... with respect to priority and seniority shall be modified' does not say how far they are modified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overrides Section 4's seniority scheme by an unspecified amount, which is precisely the kind of open-ended derogation that is hard to harmonise with 4-B and 4-E.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A bad driving record' is undefined and 'every effort' is soft; the seniority modification is again unquantified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same tension with Section 4's seniority rules as 14-B, and with 2-E.2(b)'s qualification requirements for tractor-trailer drivers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Discharged without just cause or otherwise deprived of or injured with respect to any of the rights conferred upon him hereunder' is a broad catch-all following a specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 14-A recognises discharge 'for cause' rather than 'just cause', and 16-A imposes a thirty-day referral deadline that this section does not mention.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The continuing-grievance carve-out is convoluted, and 'knew, or with reasonable diligence should have known' is a familiar but genuinely fact-sensitive standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 15 and 4-H permit submissions without mentioning any deadline, and 16-P allows extensions by agreement; whether the thirty-day bar applies to fund-contribution claims under 13-H/13-I is a live question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A composition clause with definite numbers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16-D, 16-H and 16-F; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full and complete authority, in accordance with the provisions of this section' is broad but bounded; the two-week deadline is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-K also confers powers on the Committee, and 16-D provides automatic referral on failure to act — a coherent scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear automatic-referral mechanism.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 allows a party to go straight to the Appeals Board for change-of-condition claims, an express exception rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Selected by random method agreeable to the parties' and the availability condition create a selection process that can deadlock, but the wording is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.5 requires the Impartial Chairman to be the fifth member in change-of-condition cases, an exception to this random-selection rule, and 16-G ties chairmen's terms to the Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger is garbled: 'no arbitrator listed ... is available to hear the case within thirty days after his selection' presupposes a selection that has not occurred, and it cites '16-E.1' for a list actually compiled under 16-E.2.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.2 is the list-compiling provision, so the internal cross-reference is wrong, and the Union-only election right is asymmetric against 16-E.1(a)'s joint procedure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and mechanical, though the final paragraph refers replacements to 'the procedures of 16-E.2 above' from within 16-E.2 itself — a self-referential loop.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-E.1 refers to 'the list compiled in accordance with 16-E.2' while 16-E.1's own text is cited elsewhere as the list provision, so the cross-references are inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear striking rights on fixed dates, though '1988' is a scanning error for 1983.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'the existing list of fifteen arbitrators in paragraph 16-E.1' when the list is created by 16-E.2 — the same misdirected cross-reference as 16-E.1(b).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise quorum rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16-D's five-member Board and 16-J's failure-to-appear rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence; the reference to 'permanent impartial chairmen' in the plural against 16-M's singular appointment is a small looseness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.1/16-M.2 provide for a Chairman and an Alternate serving annual terms, which the plural here presumably captures; a side letter continues the incumbents until replacements are chosen.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Exclusive jurisdiction over any issue arising with regard to the provisions of Section 4-A' is clear on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-H routes questions about qualifications and the interpretation of Section 4 to the Joint Standing Committee and Appeals Board, which contradicts the Adjustment Board's stated exclusivity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad rule-making power with a no-record default; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16-E.1(a)'s reference to the parties' adopted arbitration rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A default-hearing rule with a three-day notice threshold; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16-I and 16-C; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall include, but shall not be limited to' followed by enumerated remedies is precisely the general-plus-specific structure whose reach courts have to bound, and 'to safeguard the rights of ... other person' is unusually open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-C limits the Committee to authority 'in accordance with the provisions of this section', and 16-M.5 limits the change-of-conditions Board to that issue unless both parties consent — both cut against this expansive grant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short waiver of oath requirements; the omission of Appeals Board members from the list is notable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-D and 16-E create the Appeals Board and its chairman, who are not covered by this waiver — an expressio unius gap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Dates and terms are laid out precisely; 'until March 30, 1982' and the annual March 31–March 30 cycle are consistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-G ties chairmen's terms to expiry of the Agreement and a side letter continues the present 'status quo arbitrator' until replaced, which qualifies this schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Incapacitated or otherwise unable or unwilling to serve' and the parenthetical temporary-period exception are workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16-M.1 and 16-M.5; a side letter also continues the alternate 'status quo arbitrator'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No change in condition' is the central undefined term of the clause, and it cites 'Section 8-D' for layoffs when the layoff provision is 3-D.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mis-citation to 8-D (Chapel Chairman inspection rights) rather than 3-D is a cross-reference error, and a separate memorandum directs an arbitrator to write a decision interpreting 16-M's language — evidence the term needed construing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The thirty-day switch is clear but the asymmetry (only the Union may seek restoration) and 'prior existing conditions' as a benchmark are open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the operational corollary of 16-M.3's undefined 'change in condition' and is the subject of the same 'Applicable Status Quo Provision' memorandum.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final sentence is garbled and the limitation ('may only hear and decide the merits of the underlying grievances ... with the consent of both parties') is grammatically awkward but intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves change-of-condition cases out of 16-E.1's random arbitrator selection, so the two selection regimes must be kept apart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other cessation of work or interference therewith' is a general catch-all after named specifics, and the exception for non-compliance is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 11-A imposes a parallel assistance ban for non-compliance and 17-C requires observance of the spirit of the Agreement; the memoranda on damage awards for past work stoppages show the clause's practical bite.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple cost-sharing rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16-E and 16-M appointment provisions; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence permitting extension by mutual agreement; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It softens 16-A's thirty-day waiver rule as intended; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The quoted italic text is itself corrupted mid-sentence ('such men to be comtion for which they are required'), and the clause both prints and disclaims a provision, an inherently confusing device.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The italicised 2-L conflicts with the operative 2-L.1 to 2-L.3 that bear the same numbering, and its last sentence (no non-member may fill a regular situation) contradicts 4-A.2(g)'s permission for foremen to hire off-list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No longer is held to be inoperative' is a double negative that reverses the apparent intent, and 'court of highest resource' is a garbled phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It automatically reinstates the italicised closed-shop text, which would then contradict the operative 2-L.1's 'maximum Union security permissible' formulation and 2-N.3's agency-fee scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but carefully staged separability mechanism with clear consequences; 'to the best knowledge and belief of the parties' is a soft opening but not operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-A.5 has a narrower conformity rule for hiring practices and 13-A.5 gives a termination right rather than mere inoperativeness for wage controls — three different responses to legal conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The spirit as well as the letter' is an invitation to purposive argument, and 'renders impossible or inoperative any provisions' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-M expressly permits the parties to agree to different terms for other publishers and 17-B contemplates provisions becoming inoperative, both in tension with this absolute undertaking.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A zipper-style acknowledgment; the opening word is missing its 'b' but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Several side letters commit the parties to continue discussing pensions and other subjects during the term, which sits against the statement that all subjects have been settled for the term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Merger, consolidation, or permanent suspension by any newspaper' and 'any other money due them' are broad, and 'permanent' suspension is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12-D.1 caps a Publisher's suspension and merger pay liability to wholesaler employees at 15 days while this gives 40 shifts to the Publisher's own holders, and 4-A.2(b) Group 1 listing also flows from suspension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall be treated by the Union and each such Publisher as an individual agreement between them' is a striking characterisation of a multi-employer document; the term dates are precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble makes the Association the agent binding both Publishers and 16-B/16-O treat the Association as a party, which is hard to square with the individual-agreement characterisation — a live issue for multiemployer fund liability.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Thirty (36) days' is an internal numeric error, and 'either party may give ... notice' is permissive where a reopener would normally be mandatory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 19(b) explains the seventy-five-day figure by contrast with sixty-five days, which does not appear anywhere in (a) — the two subsections do not fully cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A purely explanatory statement of hope, with no operative content, and it references a 'sixty-five days' rule not found in the contract.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a recital-like gloss on 19(a)'s seventy-five-day notice, and the sixty-five-day baseline it assumes is absent from the operative text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two different payout rates are given in consecutive sentences — 'normal straight-time weekly pay' and 'the rate he receives for the majority of his shifts' — without a clear division between them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-K.2 says accumulated leave is paid 'at the then prevailing rate' and prescribes December payment for unaccumulated days, which is a third formulation of the same entitlement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to study and define; it creates no enforceable standard and leaves 'clerical work ... appropriate to the deliverer's bargaining unit' undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-A.1 and 2-B already purport to fix unit coverage, so a study to define a category of work sits uneasily with those recognition clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Overtime which would normally be assigned to employees who are paid a higher rate' is vague as to what is 'normal'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-M requires overtime to be worked as the employer requires and allows unfair-distribution challenges; 13-A's group rate tiers supply the higher-rate reference.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(discounting the vacation period before or after the holiday)' is opaque, and the closing proviso about foreman discretion does not obviously connect to the holiday-pay rule it qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 7-D for qualification but to 13-B.4 for entitlement, and 13-B.2 says vacations are scheduled at the employer's convenience 'but on the basis of seniority' whereas this gives the Foreman discretion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding any provision to the contrary' plus 'eliminate, reduce or phase-out' is broad but the override is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly displaces conflicting terms of the Agreement for bulldog phase-outs, which is a designed override of Sections 3 and 4 rather than a hidden conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare notice requirement with no time period specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A separate memorandum requires thirty days' notice of any major operational change, which supplies a period this clause omits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The no-layoff promise is conditioned on the situation 'having been designated as an excess situation', which the Publisher controls under 20-E.4 — a circularity within the memorandum.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-D.1's economic layoff right and 20-E.6's carve-out for holders aged seventy or more qualify this guarantee.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'No longer required because of such elimination, reduction or phasing-out' leaves the designation largely to the Publisher's judgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 20-E.3 and 20-E.5 it gives the Publisher control of the trigger for the very protection those clauses confer — the Lovejoy-style discretion problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear queue rule for filling vacancies with excess situation holders.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It displaces 4-B's posting and bidding procedure and 4-A.2(c)'s promotion order without saying so expressly, relying on 20-E.1's blanket override.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Other available work described in Section 2 ... for which they are qualified' is broad but bounded by the Section 2 list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-I permits assignment across operations and 4-A.4 requires competence, both consistent with this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing clause is garbled ('except as to excess situation holders who are seventy or more years of age nor shall the provisions of Sections 3 and 4 ... be applicable to them'), leaving unclear which men lose Section 3 and 4 protection.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies Sections 3 and 4 to a class of employees, directly overriding the layoff and seniority rules in 3-D.1 and 4-E for them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At the discretion of the Publishers' for starting times and days off is a broad grant, though its purpose is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-J requires four days' notice of starting-time and day-off changes with penalty pay, and a Times supplementary agreement guarantees present starting times — both cut against this discretion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Times will continue its present practice' leaves half the clause without ascertainable content while imposing a precise 48-hour rule on The News.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The asymmetry between the two Publishers is deliberate and mirrors Sections 21 and 22; no direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Circular in effect: questions 'which are subject to arbitration under the contract and which are submitted to arbitration will be arbitrated under Section 16'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16 already governs all such disputes, so this adds nothing and its purpose is obscure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Its own present press equipment' and 'what are currently known as' fix obligations by reference to an undocumented state of affairs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-B.4 states that this all-advertising-sections agreement ended effective March 30, 1975, so its presence in a 1981–84 contract is itself incoherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific conditional obligation for three named holidays; clear on its own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-B.4 declares the all-advertising-sections agreement expired in 1975, yet the final memorandum says every memorandum or side agreement is continued and 'deemed updated' — an unresolved contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An elaborate alternating on/off schedule keyed to 1974–75 quarters, reproduced in a 1981–84 agreement where it can have no application.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its dates are wholly spent and 21-B.4 says the arrangement ended in 1975, while the closing memorandum purports to continue and update every side agreement.
